person_made_it: A two player race for one specific couch: David on the left half, Trent on the right, Gordon's exact challenge in the opening text, Baku's castle squeeze and shoreline straight drawn into the track shape.
emcee_who_is_speaking: Gordon issues the challenge on the start screen, the game keeps score in his terms (the best and the most fabulous), and the finish screen reports to him by name.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Night race: near-black ground, magenta walls that glow, teal and magenta cars, a teal wash where the Caspian would be, the same palette as the dossier so the two pages are one object.
did_the_click_pay_me: Lights out starts a real race with wall collisions, screen shake, laps counted and two trophies awarded on distinct rules, then Race again resets in one tap.
works_for_the_recipient: Touch regions are halves and quarters so thumbs cannot miss, multi-touch is tracked per finger, a portrait overlay asks for landscape, safe areas are respected, and keyboard keys exist for desktop testing.
taught_me_something: Style points only accrue near a wall at speed, so the fabulous line and the fast line are the same line until you overcook it, which is also the truth about Baku.
told_me_the_truth: The track is Baku-shaped, not Baku-accurate, and the page says so; the physics are arcade and auto-throttle, stated up front.
weakest: No sound yet; a chiptune engine note and a wall thud would make the couch louder, and the AI has no third car to race against if one of them puts the phone down.
